content:
When pain, stiffness and frailty make leaving home very hard, getting to the GP can feel impossible.

This guide explains your options. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

When home visits are offered

Home visits are usually for people who are housebound or too unwell to travel. The practice decides based on clinical need.

How to ask

  • Call early in the day.
  • Explain why you cannot travel.
  • Describe your symptoms clearly.

Other options

  • Phone or video appointments.
  • Community nursing.
  • Pharmacy advice.
  • Help with transport.

Preparing for a visit

  • Have your medicines list ready.
  • Write down your questions.
  • Have someone with you if helpful.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, severe breathlessness, signs of stroke or a serious injury.
  • Call NHS 111 if you need urgent advice and cannot reach your practice.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Will they always visit?

Not always; it depends on need.

Can a carer call for me?

Yes, with your permission.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: GP appointments and bookings
  • British Geriatrics Society: Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment toolkit

Educational information for people in the United Kingdom — not a diagnosis or personal medical advice. Charity no. 1218461. Reviewed by Louis Maxwell (HCPC PH128483). Living With Arthritis is an independent charity and is not part of Arthritis UK (formerly Versus Arthritis). Everyone's situation is different, so follow the advice of your own GP and care team. If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
